children: Shares of Atul Ltd. are in focus on Friday, November 20, after the company said the US Customs is investing the company's unit over alleged duty evasion of 2, 4-D imports.

The company said the US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) initiated the probe based on the suspension that Chinese 2, 4-Dichlorophenoxyacetic Acid and its derivatives were transshipped to the US via India, warranting higher AD and CVD.
The investigation is initiated against Atul USA Inc to ascertain the alleged evasion of anti-dumping duty (AD) and Countervailing Dut (CVD) on 2,4-D and its derivatives.

As an interim measure, the CBP has suspended the liquidation of each unliquidated entry of such covered merchandise that entered into the US after August 11, 2026, or as permitted by law, the company said. The CBP may also take additional measures necessary to protect the revenue of the United States, the company added.
Prima facie, Atul Ltd. has denied the allegation. It said the impact is uncertain at this stage. The company has engaged US-based lawyers to seek advice and guidance in the matter.
Atul shares ended the previous session 1.2% up at ₹5,080 apiece. The stock has fallen 15.7% in the past month, 27.4% in the last six months and 17.7% this year, so far.

title: Atul shares in focus as US Customs investigates unit over alleged duty evasion
